title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol: creation of Judas is not a medium subordinated to his damnation — Augustine and Prosper; to create a reprobate ≠ to create that he may be damned
pass_a_gloss: The Jesuits were able to understand how the creation of singular angels made in time did not fight with the reprobation of certain ones, constituted from eternity by the sole will of God: they were able to conceive the same concerning men: Let Corvinus bend the edge of his wit, and he will easily understand the same. But he thinks he can confirm the consequence by this argumentation: Creation by its nature is a communication of good: But if such a reprobation as we place shall have preceded, it will be a certain way by which reprobation already before made may attain its end, it will be a medium of the non-elect man subordinated unto damnation. And therefore it will not be a communication of good; since good ought to be estimated from the mind of the giver, and from the end on account of which it is given. But these things are disputed with little solidity. For first the creation of singular men follows both their election and their reprobation. As therefore the creation of Peter would improperly be called a medium subordinated unto his election, so also the creation of Judas is improperly and falsely called a medium subordinated either unto his reprobation or unto his damnation. If there are any who dare to maintain that the creation of men is a medium subordinated unto their damnation, I dissent from them, and embrace the sentence of Augustine and Prosper, who everywhere oppose this.
pass_b_english: The Jesuits could see how the creation of particular angels in time did not fight the reprobation of some, set from eternity by God's will alone — and they could conceive the same of men. Let Corvinus bend his wit's edge, and he will easily see it. But he thinks he can shore up the consequence thus: Creation by nature is a communication of good; yet if such reprobation as we place preceded, it will be a path by which reprobation already made reaches its end — a medium of the non-elect man subordinated to damnation — and so will not be a communication of good, since good is to be judged from the giver's mind and the end for which it is given. That is weakly argued. First: creation of particular men follows both their election and their reprobation. As Peter's creation would improperly be called a medium subordinated to his election, so Judas's creation is improperly and falsely called a medium subordinated to his reprobation or damnation. If any dare hold that men's creation is a medium subordinated to their damnation, I dissent and embrace Augustine and Prosper, who everywhere oppose that.
source_text: Potuerunt Jesuitae intelligere, quomodo creatio singulorum angelorum facta in tempore non pugnaverit cum reprobatione quorundam, sola Dei voluntate ab aeterno constituta: potuerunt idem de hominibus concipere: Intendat aciem ingenii sui Corvinus, et idem facile intelligat. Sed putat se confirmare posse consequentiam hac argumentatione: Creatio sua natura est communicatio boni: At praecesserit talis reprobatio qualem nos ponimus, erit via quaedam per quam reprobatio jam ante facta finem suum consequatur, erit medium hominis non-electi damnationi subordinatum. Ac proinde non erit communicatio boni; cum bonum aestimari debeat ex mente dantis, et fine propter quem datur. Sed haec parum solide disputantur. Nam primo creatio singularium hominum tam electionem quam reprobationem eorundem consequitur. Sicuti ergo creatio Petri improprie diceretur medium subordinatum ejus electioni, ita et creatio Judae improprie et falso dicitur medium subordinatum aut reprobationi aut damnationi ejusdem. Si qui sunt qui audeant sustinere creationem hominum esse medium damnationi eorundem subordinatum, ego ab illis dissentio, et amplector sententiam Augustini et Prosperi, qui hoc passim adversantur.
